subject.title: Android: gateway pairing UX trails iOS (duplicate buttons, no discovered list, buried setup code)

question: Should Android pairing remain canonically owned by the Connect tab, with Settings linking into shared pairing actions, or should Settings become the canonical full pairing surface and replace the corresponding Connect controls?
rationale: Both designs can improve first-run UX, but the current README and runbook intentionally assign pairing to Connect while the linked PR builds a second full implementation in Settings; code inspection cannot choose that permanent navigation and ownership contract.

options.title: Keep Connect Canonical
options.body: Retain Setup Code, QR, discovery, and manual connection ownership in Connect while giving Settings a prominent shared pairing CTA plus gateway facts and diagnostics.

options.title: Move Pairing To Settings
options.body: Adopt the iOS-style Settings flow as canonical, remove or narrow the competing Connect controls, and update Android documentation and screenshot coverage together.

recommendation.title: Keep Connect Canonical
recommendation.body: Retain Setup Code, QR, discovery, and manual connection ownership in Connect while giving Settings a prominent shared pairing CTA plus gateway facts and diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository explicitly identifies @obviyus as the Android app owner, and this choice governs Android navigation and pairing ownership.
